question_text:
A 7-month-old girl is brought to the hospital by her mother, who complains of a lesion on the infant’s labia for the past 5 days. The lesion is 2 x 2 cm in size and red in color with serosanguinous fluid oozing out of the right labia. The parents note that the girl has had a history of recurrent bacterial skin infections with no pus but delayed healing since birth. She also had delayed sloughing of the umbilical cord at birth. Complete blood count results are as follows:
Neutrophils on admission  
Leukocytes 19,000/mm3
Neutrophils 83%
Lymphocytes 10%
Eosinophils 1%
Basophils 1%
Monocytes 5%
Hemoglobin 14 g/dL
Which of the following compounds is most likely to be deficient in this patient?

The high leukocyte count and elevated neutrophil percentage indicate a response to infection but also suggest a defect in leukocyte trafficking. This aligns with a deficiency in cellular adhesion molecules, which are crucial for leukocyte migration to sites of infection. The evidence path regarding impaired wound healing due to bacterial infections supports this interpretation. Deficiencies in selectins and integrins are also plausible, but the most likely deficiency given the clinical presentation is in cellular adhesion molecules, as they directly impact the ability of neutrophils to reach and respond to infections effectively.
